speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) in each of the past five years, how much Government funding has been provided for public service broadcasting (PSB); (b) which PSB programmes has received such Government funding; and (c) whether the Ministry has assessed a need to recalibrate the amount of Government funding provided in order to boost the popularity of locally created content.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the Ministry tracks data and statistics on viewership ratings of public service broadcasting (PSB) programmes; and (b) if so, how do the viewership ratings of PSB programmes in the past five years compare with those in the earlier preceding five years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They provide trusted and timely sources of information to form a common basis for social discourse.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They also reflect our multicultural fabric and way of life.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To enable our PSM entities to effectively adapt and innovate in the fast-changing media landscape, the Government provides funding for their overall operations, rather than individual programmes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: More than 75% of its audiences were satisfied with its services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not have comparable reach data in the earlier years as we have moved from tracking solely television (TV) reach to a broader reach metric across all Mediacorp's platforms and social media platforms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is in keeping with the domestic audiences' changing consumption habits and Mediacorp's broader network strategy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Meanwhile, public satisfaction with Mediacorp has held steady, at more than 75% across this time period.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government is committed to continue supporting our PSM to deliver high-quality and trusted news and entertainment content to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to ensure that Government funding can adequately and effectively support our PSM in achieving their national mission.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Speaker, Sir, I grew up watching Channel 8 and Channel 5, as did many of my classmates.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These were hot discussion topics during lunch, but most importantly, these were core common memories grounded in the local culture and community.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think it is absolutely critical that we continue to have this for future generations.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand the challenges of growing demands and competition, such as Netflix, but in particular, there were three developments recently that left me very encouraged.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mediacorp's Emerald Hill, the Little Nyonya story, I note, was Singapore's most watched series on Netflix, even overtaking hot K-dramas starring starring IU when it first debuted.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It had more than 1.67 million views on meWATCH and Channel 8, and it is going to premiere on Chinese streaming platform Tencent at the end of this year.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We have had many actors, local actors, nominated for Best Actor/Actresses at the Golden Horse Awards, and I am also looking forward to the return of Xie Shaoguang to the silver screen later.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, contrary to what naysayers say, I think the future is bright and we have to give this a further boost.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, my question for the Minister is: is the Government prepared to support Mediacorp, our local broadcaster, in more collaborations with international platforms, such as Netflix and Tencent, so that our local produced dramas and shows will have a reach both local and overseas?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I realise that he and I share something in common now.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Growing up on local TV productions, we probably can hum several tunes together, given the right opportunity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He is right that there is a need to support such local production initiatives and he mentioned a few examples that are now available on streaming services, such as Netflix, and soon to come, Tencent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are very important to widening the reach of not just Mediacorp's productions, but also the productions of independent media content creators in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They both contribute to the vibrancy of our local ecosystem.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In that regard, I am happy to share with him that it is not just the negotiations that are commercial in nature that take place between the production houses, including Mediacorp, and streaming services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These will, obviously, have to be carried forward with a view towards making sure that there is actually demand for the productions.
